paragraphs: tip411 provides a web-based toolset that lets a law enforcement agency and the public interact with each other across multiple channels in real time. Each agency gets custom branded iPhone and Android apps that are free for the public to download. The public sends 2-way anonymous tips by text using a custom keyword, by email, through weblinks and through the agency's social media sites. Community alerts go the other way, to the agency's apps, to the public's email or text, and to its social media sites.

The site lists smart tip routing alongside the tips and apps as a headline feature, and states that the platform is FedRAMP Moderate compliant. Agencies featured in the site's news section include the Provincetown Police Department in Massachusetts, with 26 sworn officers, and the Salamanca Police Department in New York, with 17 sworn officers. The Erie County, NY Sheriff's Office, with 173 sworn deputies, and the Kokomo, IN Police Department, with 89 sworn officers, also appear there.

One testimonial, from SGT Kevin Fair, reports a little over 200 tips in the first full year of use and over 4,200 in 2018. Another, from Mayor Rita Ali, counts more than 700 tips since the program started. tip411 plans to show its anonymous tip and community engagement tools at the 2026 Midwest Security and Police Conference.

quote.text: tip411 provides a web-based toolset that allows your agency and the public to interact with each other like never before, across multiple channels, in real time, at an affordable cost.
